AbstractText.Label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To demonstrate that laparoscopic excision of the endometrial tissue of a blind endometrial cavity in a patient with a Robert's uterus who did not consent to hysteroscopic surgery due to her virgin state and religious beliefs was an effective alternative treatment option for progressive dismenorrhea and pelvic pain.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Presentation of a rare müllerian anomaly and a step-by-step demonstration of a laparoscopic excision technique in the endometrium of a blind uterine cavity (educative video) (Canadian Task Force classification III).

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Robert's uterus is a rare müllerian anomaly characterized by the presence of a blind endometrial cavity and an asymmetric septum. Endometriosis may be encountered in 40% of patients with this anomaly. A 15-year-old virgin patient with progressive dysmenorrhea was diagnosed with a Robert's uterus anomaly on magnetic resonance imaging. Hysteroscopic surgery was suggested to form a communication between the blind endometrial cavity and the hemiuterus; however, the patient refused to undergo any vaginal surgery due to her virgin state and religous beliefs. A decision to excise the endometrial tissue of the blind cavity laparoscopically instead of performing a hemihysterectomy was made to prevent any adverse effects on the ovarian blood supply and damage to the myometrial wall of the unicornuate uterus.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: Laparoscopic resection of the blind endometrial cavity in a patient with a Robert's uterus anomaly.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Laparoscopic resection of a blind endometrial cavity is a safe and effective surgical alternative in patients who refuse vaginal surgery.
